glossary.Superimposed thrombus: A blood clot forming on top of a ruptured plaque.
glossary.ST elevation: Raised ST segment on ECG, showing full-thickness myocardial injury.
glossary.ST depression: Lowered ST segment on ECG, usually showing subendocardial ischaemia.
glossary.T-wave inversion: Upside-down T wave on ECG, a sign of ischaemia.
glossary.Infarction: Tissue death caused by loss of its blood supply.
glossary.Reperfusion: Restoring blood flow through a blocked artery.
glossary.Hyperlipidaemia: Raised blood cholesterol or other fats.
glossary.Palpitations: An unpleasant awareness of one's own heartbeat.
glossary.Syncope: Brief loss of consciousness from reduced blood flow to the brain.
glossary.Atypical presentation: Presenting without the classic features, e.g. MI with breathlessness or nausea but no chest pain.
glossary.Left bundle branch block: Delayed conduction down the left bundle, producing broad QRS complexes; new LBBB can mean acute MI.
glossary.STEMI-equivalent: An ECG finding managed exactly like STEMI with urgent reperfusion.
glossary.Crackles: Fine clicking sounds on auscultation as fluid-filled airways open.
glossary.Auscultation: Listening to the body with a stethoscope.
glossary.Prognostic: Telling you about the likely outcome.
glossary.Acute heart failure: Sudden failure of the heart to pump enough, causing breathlessness and pulmonary oedema.
glossary.Echo: Echocardiogram: ultrasound scan of the heart.
glossary.Bradycardia: Heart rate below 60 beats per minute.
glossary.30-day mortality: The proportion of patients who die within 30 days.
glossary.NSAIDs: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, such as ibuprofen and naproxen.
glossary.Cocaine: Stimulant drug that causes coronary vasospasm and raises MI risk.
glossary.Serial troponins: Repeated troponin measurements over hours to detect a rise or fall.
glossary.Biomarker: A measurable substance in the blood that indicates disease.
glossary.Reinfarction: A further MI after a recent one.
glossary.Inferior MI: Infarction of the bottom wall of the left ventricle, usually from the RCA.
glossary.Anterior MI: Infarction of the front wall of the left ventricle, from the LAD.
glossary.Anterolateral: Involving both the front and side walls of the left ventricle.
glossary.Posterior MI: Infarction of the back wall of the heart, seen as ST depression in V1-V3 and elevation in V7-V9.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: blood test of kidney function and salts like sodium and potassium.
glossary.Risk-stratify: Sort patients by how likely they are to have a bad outcome, to guide treatment.
glossary.Aspirin: Antiplatelet drug that irreversibly blocks COX, reducing thromboxane and platelet clumping.
glossary.Nitrates: Drugs like GTN that dilate veins and coronary arteries to relieve angina.
glossary.Antiemetic: A drug that prevents or treats nausea and vomiting.
glossary.Antiplatelet: A drug that stops platelets clumping together.
glossary.Anticoagulated: Already taking a drug that reduces clotting, such as warfarin or a DOAC.
glossary.Apixaban: Oral anticoagulant (DOAC) that blocks factor Xa.
glossary.Warfarin: Oral anticoagulant blocking vitamin K-dependent clotting factors.
glossary.Radial artery: The wrist artery, the preferred access route for PCI.
glossary.Haemodynamic instability: Unstable blood pressure or circulation, such as hypotension or shock.
glossary.ACE inhibitor: Drug that blocks angiotensin II production, lowering BP and reducing cardiac remodelling.
glossary.Beta-blocker: Drug that slows the heart and lowers its oxygen demand.
glossary.Secondary prevention: Treatment to stop a further event in someone who has already had one.
glossary.LV dysfunction: Impaired pumping of the left ventricle.
glossary.Angioplasty: Opening a narrowed artery with a balloon, usually with a stent.
glossary.Platelet aggregation: Platelets sticking together to form a plug.
glossary.Coagulation cascade: The chain of clotting factor reactions that ends in a fibrin clot.
glossary.Myocardial oxygen demand: How much oxygen the heart muscle needs, raised by fast rate and high BP.
glossary.Diabetes: Condition of raised blood glucose from lack of or resistance to insulin.
